question: Using a standard adult blood pressure cuff to measure blood pressure in an obese 12-year-old child will systematically underestimate the true blood pressure reading.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. An inappropriately small cuff in an obese child gives FALSELY HIGH blood pressure — not an underestimate. Always use a large-size paediatric or adult cuff that covers ≥80% of upper arm circumference to avoid misdiagnosing hypertension.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Using an undersized or inappropriately sized cuff in an obese child gives a FALSELY ELEVATED (not underestimated) blood pressure reading. The cuff bladder must cover at least 80% of the upper arm circumference; a cuff that is too small for the arm overestimates blood pressure.
